channel.title: Block Club Chicago - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from Block Club Chicago (blockclubchicago.org)

item.title: Black, Hispanic Drivers Get Majority Of Chicago’s Traffic Tickets — Including In Mostly White Areas
item.description: The study comes as the Police Department negotiates a new policy around traffic stops, which reform advocates say has been widely abused by officers fishing for evidence of more serious crimes, leading to racial profiling.

item.title: For 40 Years, Black-Owned Out Of The Past Records Has Survived And Thrived On The West Side
item.description: Founded by Marie and Charlie Joe Henderson, the shop has endured for four decades on Madison Street. Their granddaughter carries on the family's legacy amid efforts to revitalize the corridor.

item.title: Smashing Pumpkins Played Their 1st Show At Club 21. Can Parts Of Closed Venue Be Saved?
item.description: In 1988, the iconic band performed their first show at Chicago 21 Club, a Polish nightclub on the Far Northwest Side. Nearly four decades later, a local historian wants to save the long-vacant clubs' ornate front doors.

item.title: 22 Things To Do In Chicago This Weekend: Nature’s Rage Room, Lunar New Year And Valentine’s Day
item.description: There's also a Black Creativity Career Showcase, a Scandinavian Jam sesh and a Community Repair Clinic.

item.title: New Humboldt Park Affordable Apartment Building Welcomes Residents: ‘I Can Breathe Now’
item.description: About 400 applications came through for the 40-unit building, which has been in the works since 2018 and was completed last year.

item.title: Chicago Trio Snags Guinness World Record For Visiting All CTA Stations
item.description: The friends set out in November to achieve the record for “Fastest Time to Travel to All Chicago Subway Stations.” The Guinness Book certified their record in December.

item.title: Cops Who Killed Dexter Reed Cleared On All But 1 Allegation As City Watchdog Closes Probe
item.description: The Civilian Office of Police Accountability investigation, which included the departure of its overseer amid pressure from the Police Department, is now on the desk of Supt. Larry Snelling, who can decide whether to discipline the officers involved.

item.title: Club Lucky’s Big Tipping Couple Leaves $4,000 On $140 Bill, Their Biggest Gratuity Yet
item.description: This is the fifth year the anonymous couple has left a massive tip, management said. They visit the Bucktown restaurant every February for their anniversary.

item.title: Illinois Wetlands Are At Risk As Federal Protections Vanish. Will State Move To Protect Them?
item.description: As the Trump administration attempts to roll back wetland protections, environmental groups are calling on state legislators to protect these vital waterways before it's too late.

item.title: Some School Board Members Claim ‘Sabotage’ As Chicago Schools And CEO Search Firm Part Ways
item.description: The termination of Alma’s contract is the latest twist in a search process that began last spring and hasn’t yet produced a permanent CEO.
